documents.title: System context
documents.plain:
walflip is a local command-line tool. It has no server and no background process; each command is one OS process and all state lives under the data root.

The operator runs every write through `walflip exec`. A CI job or fuzzer operator is a secondary consumer that runs the test suites and the WAL fuzzer.

Other programs that open `live.db` are **not supported**: their writes are not captured, and a checkpoint they cause can discard WAL frames before walflip reads them (README, Limitations).

ste.text:
walflip is a local command-line tool. Each command is one process. All data is in the data root.

The operator must send all writes through walflip exec. Other programs must not write live.db. If they write it, walflip does not record the change.

documents.title: Operator
documents.plain: Selects a database with `--db NAME` or `WALFLIP_DB`, and a data root with `--root DIR` or `WALFLIP_ROOT` (default `walflip-data`, relative to the working directory).

ste.text: Use --db or WALFLIP_DB to select the database. Use --root or WALFLIP_ROOT to select the data root.

documents.title: CLI binary
documents.plain: Subcommands: `create NAME [--schema FILE|-]`, `list`, `rename OLD NEW`, `drop NAME`, `exec SQL|-`, `log [--limit N]`, `status`, `clone -n N -o FILE`. Each arm of the `match` in `main` calls one `walflip::db` function and prints its result. After `clone`, `report` calls `db::summarize` and prints `integrity_check` and row counts.

ste.text: The CLI reads the arguments. It calls one library function for each command. It prints the result. It does not contain logic.

documents.title: Runtime containers and data stores
documents.plain:
Two code containers (the binary and the library crate) and five data stores. Four stores live in one folder per database, `ROOT/NAME/`: `live.db`, `live.db-wal`, `base.db` and `meta.db`. The fifth is the clone file at the `-o` path.

`live.db-wal` is owned by SQLite. walflip only reads it, as raw bytes, from inside `exec`.

ste.text:
The binary calls the library. The library reads and writes five files. Four files are in the database folder. The fifth file is the clone.

SQLite writes live.db-wal. walflip only reads it.

documents.title: Tests, fuzzing and tooling
documents.plain:
Each suite is a separately runnable target. In-crate `#[cfg(test)]` modules test internals. `tests/roundtrip.rs` links the library and compares clones with live contents. `tests/cli.rs` spawns the compiled binary through `tests/common::Harness`, uses a shadow-SQLite `Model` as oracle and checks the invariant catalog through the library. The fuzz crate depends on walflip with feature `testing` and calls only `wal::parse`. `scripts/seed.sh` drives the binary to build the 500-commit demo; `tests/cli.rs` also runs it.

No CI workflow exists in the repo. Planned fuzz targets and CI jobs are described in [TESTING_PLAN.md](https://github.com/nickstrad/walflip/blob/main/docs/TESTING_PLAN.md) sections 2.1 and 2.4.

ste.text:
Each test suite runs separately. The fuzz crate sends random bytes to wal::parse. The seed script runs the binary to make a demo database.

The repository has no CI file. The testing plan gives the CI jobs that are planned.

documents.title: Library components and the pure/I-O boundary
documents.plain:
Dependencies point one way: `main.rs` -> `db` -> `store` -> `wal`, and `db` -> `replay`. `wal` and `replay` import only `anyhow`; they take bytes or slices and return values. `store` and `db` own all file and SQLite I/O. `store::commits_seen` is a pure function inside the I/O module so the cursor rule can be property-tested alone.

`main.rs` is shown as a supporting component of the CLI container. Tests and the fuzz crate also call the library directly (see the verification container view).

Note: the doc comment in `src/lib.rs` still lists a `schema` module as pure. That module no longer exists; the doc comment is stale.

ste.text:
Dependencies go in one direction: main.rs, then db, then store, then wal. db also uses replay.

wal and replay do not read or write files. store and db do all file and SQLite operations.

documents.title: db module
documents.plain: Names must be 1-64 characters of ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`, because they become folder names. `parse_statements` splits stdin into one statement per non-blank line. Every function returns a plain struct (`Created`, `DbSummary`, `LogEntry`, `Status`, `Summary`) or a count.

ste.text: A database name must have 1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. The name becomes a folder name. Each function returns data. It does not print.

documents.title: Architecture decisions and constraints
documents.plain:
- **Parse the WAL file directly instead of using SQLite hooks.** `store::capture` reads `live.db-wal` with `fs::read` and `wal::parse` validates magic, page size, salts and the chained checksum. Commits are frames up to one with non-zero `db_size`.
- **Full-page replay.** Every WAL frame is a whole page, so `replay::apply` is positioned overwrites at `(pgno - 1) * page_size` on a copy of `base.db`, then a resize to commit N's `db_pages`. No SQL runs during replay.
- **Library returns data, CLI prints.** `db` returns structs; `main.rs` only formats output. Tests call the library directly.
- **Capture runs inside exec with autocheckpoint disabled.** `db::exec` sets `PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0` and calls `capture` after every commit on the same open connection, so SQLite cannot fold frames into `live.db` before they are read.
- **Cursor = salts + commit count.** `meta.cursor_salt` and `meta.cursor_commits` record the WAL generation and how many of its commits are stored. A new salt (WAL restarted after a checkpoint) resets the count to 0, so re-reading the same WAL adds nothing.
- **page_size pinned at create.** `create` stores `PRAGMA page_size` in `meta`; `capture` rejects a WAL with a different page size because replay offsets depend on it.
- **Replay allocation bound.** `clone_at` passes `max_pages = max(base pages, max db_pages over 1..=N)`; `apply` rejects any frame or size above it before changing the image.
- **One statement = one transaction = at most one commit.** A statement that changes nothing writes no frames and adds no commit.

ste.text:
- walflip reads the WAL file directly. It does not use SQLite hooks.
- Each WAL frame is a full page. Replay writes each page at its offset. Replay does not run SQL.
- The library returns data. The CLI prints the data.
- exec stops automatic checkpoints. exec reads the WAL after each commit.
- The cursor is the WAL salts and the number of commits. A new salt sets the number to 0.
- create records the page size. capture stops with an error if the WAL page size is different.

documents.title: Known gaps (reported by TESTING_PLAN.md, not re-verified)
documents.plain:
These defects are **reported by** [docs/TESTING_PLAN.md](https://github.com/nickstrad/walflip/blob/main/docs/TESTING_PLAN.md). They were not re-run for this documentation.

- **B1** (medium): `summarize` does not double `"` in table names, so `clone` writes the file and then fails on a name such as `a"b`. Affects the clone report step.
- **B2** (high): a statement that contains `COMMIT` commits to `live.db`, then `tx.commit()` fails and capture never runs; the WAL is checkpointed on close and history is lost. Affects the exec loop.
- **B3** (medium): commits already in `live.db-wal` when `exec` starts (crashed or external writer) are captured under the next statement's label.
- **B4** (high): concurrent `exec` on one database fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: commits.idx` and records extra commits; the cursor is read outside the `meta.db` transaction.
- **B5** (high): a schema with `PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE` is accepted; afterwards every `exec` captures 0 commits.
- **B6** (medium): `replay::apply` could be forced into a huge allocation by a large `pgno` or `db_pages`. Observation: the current code has a `max_pages` parameter and a test `huge_pgno_is_rejected_without_allocating`, so this looks addressed, but the plan still lists it.
- **B7** (low/UX): `PRAGMA page_size` and `PRAGMA auto_vacuum` in a schema are silently ignored because WAL mode is enabled first; `create` reports 4096.
- **B8** (low): an unterminated `BEGIN` in a schema fails with `database table is locked` instead of an "applying schema" message.

ste.text:
The testing plan reports these defects. We did not test them again.

- B1: Table names with a quote character cause the clone report to fail.
- B2: A statement with COMMIT can cause a loss of history.
- B3: Old commits in the WAL get the label of the next statement.
- B4: Two exec processes at the same time can corrupt the history.
- B5: A schema can turn off WAL mode. Then exec records no commits.
- B6: A large page number could cause a very large allocation. The current code has a limit for this.
- B7: create ignores page_size and auto_vacuum in the schema.
- B8: An open BEGIN in the schema gives an unclear error.

documents.title: WAL file format as parsed by wal::parse
documents.plain:
All header integers are big-endian u32. The magic only selects the byte order of the checksum words.

**Header, 32 bytes:** 0 magic (`0x377f0682` little-endian checksums, `0x377f0683` big-endian); 4 format version (not checked; encoder writes 3007000); 8 page size (must be a power of two and at least 512); 12 checkpoint sequence (not checked); 16 salt-1; 20 salt-2; 24 checksum-1; 28 checksum-2 (over bytes 0-23).

**Frame, 24 + page_size bytes:** 0 page number; 4 db size in pages if this is a commit frame, else 0; 8 salt-1; 12 salt-2; 16 checksum-1; 20 checksum-2; 24 page image. The checksum covers frame bytes 0-7 then the page, chained from the previous frame (or the header).

**Outcomes:** buffer shorter than 32 bytes or bad header checksum gives `Ok(None)`; bad magic or page size gives `Err`; the frame loop stops at the first salt mismatch (older generation), checksum mismatch or partial frame; frames after the last commit frame are dropped.

ste.text:
The header has 32 bytes. It has the magic number, the page size, two salts and a checksum.

Each frame has a 24-byte header and one page. The frame header has the page number, the database size, the salts and a checksum.

A frame with a database size that is not zero ends a commit. The parser stops at the first bad salt or bad checksum.

documents.title: meta.db schema
documents.plain:
- `meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)`: keys `page_size`, `cursor_salt` (`salt1:salt2`), `cursor_commits`.
- `commits(idx INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, label TEXT NOT NULL, db_pages INTEGER NOT NULL, committed_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)`: `idx` is 1-based; `label` is the SQL statement.
- `frames(commit_idx INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES commits(idx), seq INTEGER NOT NULL, pgno INTEGER NOT NULL, page BLOB NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(commit_idx, seq))`.

`Store::open` runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on every open, so `list`, `status` and `log` create an empty `meta.db` if it is missing. Each `capture` writes its commits, frames and cursor in one transaction.

ste.text:
meta.db has three tables: meta, commits and frames. meta keeps the page size and the cursor. commits has one row for each commit. frames keeps the page images.

Each capture writes all rows in one transaction.

documents.title: create --schema
documents.plain:
The name is validated before the schema file is read. WAL mode is switched on **before** the schema runs, then the WAL is checkpointed with `TRUNCATE` so `base.db` is a complete, WAL-free copy. If any step in `init_files` fails, `create` removes the whole folder.

Failure cases: folder already exists; schema SQL error (folder removed). Reported gaps: B5 (schema can switch journal mode away from WAL), B7 (`page_size`/`auto_vacuum` in the schema ignored), B8 (unterminated `BEGIN` gives a locking error).

ste.text: create checks the name first. Then it reads the schema. It sets WAL mode before it runs the schema. Then it copies live.db to base.db. If a step fails, create removes the folder.

documents.title: exec: WAL parse and idempotent capture
documents.plain:
Invariant: capture runs on the same open connection, after each commit, with automatic checkpointing off, so every committed frame is still in the WAL when it is read.

The cursor makes capture idempotent: `seen = commits_seen(cursor_salt, cursor_commits, wal.salt)`; only commits after `seen` are inserted, and the cursor is set to the WAL's total. When `exec` returns the connection closes; SQLite then normally checkpoints and removes the WAL, and the next `exec` starts a new generation with new salts, so the count restarts at 0.

Failure cases: `--db` missing or unknown; SQL error (earlier statements stay committed and captured); WAL page size differs from `meta.page_size`. Reported gaps: B2 (`COMMIT` inside a statement), B3 (pre-existing WAL commits mislabelled), B4 (concurrent exec; cursor read outside the transaction).

ste.text:
exec stops automatic checkpoints. After each commit, exec reads the WAL and records the new commits. The cursor tells which commits are already recorded. Thus a second read adds nothing.

Do not run two exec commands on one database at the same time.

documents.title: clone -n N: replay and db_pages resize
documents.plain:
`clone_at` loads frames of commits 1..=N in `(commit_idx, seq)` order, so later writes to a page win. `replay::apply` validates every frame before changing anything (page 0, page above `max_pages`, wrong length, `db_pages` above `max_pages` all give `Err`). After the overwrites it resizes the image to commit N's `db_pages`, which shrinks it when a later commit freed pages (for example after `DROP TABLE` with `auto_vacuum`). For N = 0 no frames apply and the result is `base.db`.

The image is built in memory, so clone needs RAM roughly the size of the database. Failure cases: output exists; N greater than the commit count; no recorded page size. Reported gap: B1 (table names containing `"` break the report after the file is written).

ste.text: clone reads base.db into memory. It writes each stored page at its offset, in commit order. Then it sets the size to the size of commit N. Then it writes the file and checks it.

documents.title: list, status and log
documents.plain: These three commands are independent; the scenario shows them as unordered branches. All are read-only on history, but `Store::open` runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so it creates `meta.db` if it is missing. `status` reports `live wal: absent (checkpointed)` when `live.db-wal` does not exist, which is the normal state between commands.

ste.text: list, status and log only read the history. status shows if live.db-wal exists. Usually it does not exist between commands.

documents.title: Deployment: developer machine
documents.plain:
Install with `cargo install --path .` (Rust 1.75+, Unix-like OS; SQLite is bundled). Make targets: `make build` (`cargo build --release`), `make test` (`cargo test`), `make fuzz` (`cargo +nightly fuzz run wal_parse -- -max_total_time=$(FUZZ_SECS)`, default 30 s, needs nightly and cargo-fuzz), `make seed` (build, then `scripts/seed.sh` with `WALFLIP=target/release/walflip`), `make demo` (seed, then clone at 250 and 500 into `/tmp`), `make clean`, `make distclean`.

The data root defaults to `walflip-data/` in the working directory, so the installed binary and the release binary share data only when run from the same directory.

ste.text: Install walflip with cargo install. Use make build, make test, make fuzz, make seed and make demo. make fuzz needs the nightly Rust toolchain and cargo-fuzz.

documents.title: Deployment: CI (planned)
documents.plain: Not implemented. [TESTING_PLAN.md](https://github.com/nickstrad/walflip/blob/main/docs/TESTING_PLAN.md) section 2.4 plans a nightly job (each fuzz target for 300 s with `-rss_limit_mb=1024` and a dictionary) and a PR job (`cargo +nightly fuzz build` plus corpus replay with `-runs=0`).

ste.text: This deployment is planned. It does not exist now.
